title: Omitted point classes restrict trivially
statement: Under the hypotheses of lem-sc-pic-restriction-exact, let P be a closed point of c.Z whose underlying point is not in the image of c.i. Then Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i sends O(P), the dual point-ideal class [def-sc-invertible-module, def-sc-picard-group], to 1.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: Let J be the reduced vanishing ideal of P. Its support is {P}. The support of J.comap c.i is the inverse image of this singleton, which is empty by the boundary hypothesis. support_eq_bot_iff therefore gives J.comap c.i = top. J is invertible by the closed-point Cartier theorem; its comap is invertible as the top ideal.

The source nonempty_pullback_toModules_iso identifies the pullback of J.toModules with the module of its comap. Pic.eq_iff_nonempty_iso gives equality of their Picard classes. Rewrite O(P) as the inverse of the class of J, use map_inv, and identify the top-ideal class with 1 using Pic.ofIsInvertible_toModules_top. Thus O(P) pulls back to 1.

from.place: Affine case: restriction from the smooth compactification and the boundary kernel

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.pic_restriction_boundary_trivial
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C]
    (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g]
    [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g]
    (P : closedPoints c.Z) (hP : P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base) :
    Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i (@Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P) = 1
